description: Agent Reliability: submit a service’s failover arrangement record with the continuity claims in its terms or listing: the arrangement with the service, the standby (active-active, hot, warm, cold or none), where the standby runs, the recovery time and recovery point objectives in minutes, each condition that starts failover and whether failover starts without a person; the claims with the service, the standby, the objectives, the conditions and whether failover is automatic as the terms or listing state them. The signed report gives the arrangement and the claims, the standby ranked from none to active-active, both objectives, the conditions matched both ways and the activation on each side, and counts them, and names a divergent arrangement: a standby weaker than claimed, a recovery time or recovery point longer than claimed, a claimed failover condition the arrangement does not hold and a manual failover where the claim is automatic; then a stronger standby, shorter objectives, conditions the claims leave out, automatic failover the claims do not mention and another service, with the fix for each and what would change the verdict. No standby, no recovery time or recovery point on either side, or no conditions on either side leaves the arrangement unverified. Objectives compare in minutes to the tenth and conditions by their words. This reads a service’s arrangement against what it tells its buyers: wever_incident-plan-check reads your own incident response plan for coverage and gaps, wever_incident-ownership-check reads an operations roster of owners, responders and per-agent fallbacks, wever_recovery-readiness-check reads your own backup, key recovery and restore arrangements before you depend on them, wever_continuity-check reads an operator’s continuity plan, and wever_cyber-backup-check reads backup and restore records against a backup policy, while the failover check reads one service’s standby, objectives and triggers against the continuity claims that service makes to its buyers. Verdict rely_failover_divergent, rely_failover_partial, rely_failover_unverified or rely_failover_consistent. POST /api/rely-failover-check. Reads the reliability records supplied in the call and returns a signed report with the verdict, the evidence read, the findings with their fixes, and what would change the verdict; it reads consistency between documents only: it never probes, pings or measures a live service or endpoint, computes no service credit and names no amount owed, verifies nothing with outside sources and judges no service’s actual reliability, only whether its records agree with each other and with what it advertises, and the records stay in the report, with no network request, fetch, message, payment or external write. Agent Reliability reads a service’s reliability records for consistency between documents: an uptime report, an error budget record, a failover arrangement, a dependency disclosure, a degradation behavior record, an incident history, a maintenance record and a periodic reliability report, each against the log, SLO, terms, listing, advertised behavior, buyer disclosure, policy or records it should agree with. Beside it, wever_endpoint-reliability-check and wever_endpoint-honesty-check probe one live endpoint at one moment for the Endpoint reliability page, and the DiligenceOps reads such as wever_sla-evidence-check and wever_status-evidence-check restate one document on its own, while this family connects to nothing and reads the records in the call against each other and against what the service advertises. Paid URL: 0.10 USDC per call on Base via x402 exact, with the shared 10 signed-wallet free calls per rolling 30 days. Bind X-Wever-Wallet-Proof to the exact JSON arguments and the tool route. Returns a report with an Ed25519 signed receipt. Contract: /api/agent-reliability-contract. Human page: https://weverlabs.com/agent-reliability/.
